headline: Respect for a woman’s dignity not just a matter of personal morality but constitutional obligation: Supreme Court
description: Court rejects plea of former Intelligence Bureau employee against his compulsory retirement over allegation that he set his wife on fire.
author: Nasir Iqbal
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court (SC) stated on Tuesday that respect for a woman’s dignity was not merely a matter of personal morality but a constitutional obligation the state expected of everyone in its service.

The declaration came as a two-member bench, headed by Justice Ayesha Malik and including Justice Shahid Waheed, rejected a plea filed by a former employee of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) against his compulsory retirement over the allegation that he had set his wife on fire.

“Off-duty conduct of sufficient gravity may constitute misconduct and acquittal in a criminal case does not undo misconduct independently established in departmental proceedings,” affirmed Justice Shahid Waheed in the nine-page judgement authored by him.

The plea was filed by Jawad Abbasi, who used to work as a cook in the IB, against a Jan 15 decision by the Federal Service Tribunal’s (FST) to uphold his compulsory retirement from service.

He had faced disciplinary proceedings under the Civil Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2020 over allegations that he had set his wife on fire and was ill-mannered and short-tempered. Abbasi was also accused of conduct that was criminal, unprofessional and prejudicial to good order and service discipline. Moreover, his conduct was said to have adversely affected the reputation and discipline of the IB.

The departmental proceedings found the charges established, and by an order dated June 14, 2024, he was penalised with compulsory retirement. His departmental appeal in the case had also been rejected, and his appeal pertaining to his service had been dismissed by the FST.

However, lower court acquitted him in the criminal case in the matter.

Before the SC, his counsel Aftab Alam Yasir argued that the matter at hand was a private and domestic one between the married couple, had no connection with the petitioner’s official duties, and that Abbasi’s conduct outside his workplace and office hours could not constitute misconduct under the Civil Servants Rules.

The counsel pointed out that his client had previously been acquitted by a trial court, further claiming that his wife had attempted suicide. He contended that the rejection of Abbasi’s plea following the departmental inquiry was erroneous.

In his judgement on the matter, Justice Waheed observed that the dignity of a woman, whether as a wife, sister, daughter, mother or a fellow citizen, was a fundamental value protected by the Constitution.

“Respect for that dignity is not merely a matter of personal morality; it is an obligation that the state is entitled to expect from every person in its service,” the judgement said.

It added that the conduct of a civil servant was not judged exclusively by the manner in which he performed his official duties. His character, integrity and conduct in private life may also become relevant where these factors bore upon his suitability to hold a public office, the discipline of the service or public confidence in the institution he served, Justice Waheed emphasised.

A person’s conduct towards those within his own home may, in appropriate circumstances, reveal qualities of character that could not be disregarded merely because the conduct occurred beyond the workplace, the judgement said.

“The walls of a home are not a jurisdictional boundary, and violence does not become private because it is committed behind a closed door,” Justice Waheed stated, adding that “fire does not become a family affair because it was lit indoors”.

“The allegation is not of a quarrel or a harsh word. It is that the petitioner set his wife on fire, an act which, if established, is among the gravest forms of violence one person can inflict upon another,” the judgement said.

It further stated: “It is no incident of married life; it is an assault on life and the dignity of a human being.”

The court also observed that the first information report (FIR) in the case was registered under Section 324 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), which carried the penalty for an attempt to murder, and that burn injuries to the woman independently attracted the provisions on hurt in Chapter XVI (offences affecting the human body) of the PPC.

The legislature had classified such conduct as a public wrong against the state, not a private dispute to be settled between spouses, the judgement said, adding that the right to life under Article 9 of the Constitution and the inviolability of the dignity of a person under Article 14 protected a wife within her home as fully as any citizen in a public place.

“The Constitution does not stop at the threshold of a home; it walks in with every woman who lives there,” the judgement said.

Moreover, Article 25(3) permitted special provision for the protection of women, and the legislature had acted upon it through, among other enactments, the Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2016 and the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2020 for the Islamabad Capital Territory, the court observed.

In addition, Pakistan was a party to the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women, under which violence against women was recognised as a form of discrimination that the state must act to eliminate, the judgement said.

“The burning of women in their homes, frequently passed off as a kitchen or stove accident or as attempted suicide, is a grave and recurring social evil in this country,” stated Justice Waheed.

“The plea of suicide is often the final injury inflicted upon a burnt woman; having been robbed of her safety, she is then robbed of the truth, and her suffering is recast as her own doing,” he said in the judgement, adding that a public institution could not remain unconcerned about such an allegation against one of its own employees and that indifference would be a failure of institutional duty, not a mark of respect for privacy.

“Conduct of this gravity bears directly on the petitioner’s suitability for public service. A civil servant found, on proper inquiry, to have used potentially lethal violence against his own spouse displays a want of self-control and a disregard for human life,” the court declared.

It observed that such conduct was “wholly unbecoming” of a government servant and prejudicial to good order and service discipline.

“Where he then seeks to escape responsibility by casting the blame upon the victim, claiming that she set herself alight, he adds deceit to violence. A man who sets his wife on fire and then calls it her suicide has failed twice, first as a husband and then as a witness to the truth; such a man cannot be called a gentleman,” the court ruled.

The judgement said public confidence in the civil service rested on the assurance that those who served the state respected the dignity of those around them and a civil servant who denied that respect to his own wife forfeited the trust on which his office depended.

“Public service is a trust, and the conduct of those who hold it is a matter of public concern, at home as much as at work,” the judgement said. “Respect for women is not a private virtue that a civil servant may practise or neglect as he pleases; it is part of the character [of] the state.”

headline: Govt enlists oil refineries to shield citizens from global price hikes
description: Says they will bear a burden of Rs15bn for 30 days, which will allow petrol to be sold at Rs15 less than the global market.
author: News Desk
article_text:
The government said on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 billion for a month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The statement came at a press conference in Islamabad addressed by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Addressing the conference, Malik said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had made efforts to meet with oil refineries and consult with them regarding interventions to ensure that people got the cheapest petrol amid impending steep fuel price increases, including an increase of about Rs15 that would have taken effect on Friday.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme announced by the premier on Sept 13, saying: “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service.

However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

The two ministers also stressed that there was no fuel shortage and that the country’s needs were being met even during difficult times. Malik said that November’s supply was fully covered, while decisions would be taken on supplies for the winter months of December and January and the prime minister had directed any necessary steps to be taken to ensure supplies.

The price of high speed diesel has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

As of July, fuel prices are now fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme announced by the premier on Sept 13, saying: “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service.

However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

The two ministers also stressed that there was no fuel shortage and that the country’s needs were being met even during difficult times. Malik said that November’s supply was fully covered, while decisions would be taken on supplies for the winter months of December and January and the prime minister had directed any necessary steps to be taken to ensure supplies.

The price of high speed diesel has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

As of July, fuel prices are now fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices.

The Israeli military has said it had no involvement in reported US strikes on an Iranian island, despite PM Benjamin Netanyahu’s recent threats to resume war with Tehran, AFP reports.

Asked if Israel was involved in secret attacks reported by US media outlets on Qeshm Island, which lies in the Strait of Hormuz, an Israeli military spokespeson told AFP, “No”.

headline: Foreign women rape case: Incomplete police report clears five suspects of sexual assault charges
description: Police charge three other suspects, who are allegedly low-paid employees of one of the prime suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
article_text:
LAHORE: An incomplete investigation report (challan) filed before a trial court in connection with the alleged gang rape of two foreign women in July cleared five suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, of sexual assault charges.

However, the report implicated them in other offences, including illegal detention and extortion.

The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.

Defence C police registered the first information report (FIR) under Sections 365-A (kidnapping or abducting for extorting property, valuable security), 375-A (rape), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence), 368 (wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person) and 337-L (II) (punishment for other hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) in July.

The investigation report said the two complainants alleged that they had met one of the three prime suspects in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.

After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested a further $500,000. However, according to the police report, the women did not pay him any profits or return his investment this time.

In June this year, the suspect invited the foreign women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to Murree and other areas.

The investigation report alleged that the suspect subsequently told an associate that the women owed him money. The associate then involved another prime suspect, identified as “boss”.

On June 29, the women were taken to a house in Defence Phase VII, Lahore, where they were allegedly detained and pressured to pay the amount.

Police said the women were forced to transfer around $19,500, which was converted into rupees through a Lahore-based account. Of this amount, Rs1.1 million each reportedly went to two of the suspects.

According to the report submitted to the court, the women alleged that armed men guarded them at the house, threatened them with a knife, a gun and a piece of broken mirror, and warned that they would be killed and their body parts sold if they failed to meet the demands.

The report said the complainants’ statements and the investigation indicated that three suspects had committed sexual assault. Police said they found no evidence of rape against the other five suspects, including the relative of the political figure and the suspect identified as “boss”.

The report further stated that the women escaped on July 1 when a car taking them to the airport met with an accident near Bhatta Chowk.

They raised an alarm, following which the relative of the senior political figure fled, and the police took the women into their protection.

Police also claimed to have recovered Rs4.3 million allegedly extorted from the women, along with a mobile phone and a vehicle allegedly used in the crime. Pistols and a rifle were also recovered, leading to the registration of separate cases under the Arms Ordinance, the report added.

Another suspect was accused of renting the house to the group without informing the authorities, while a further suspect was allegedly involved in helping to destroy evidence.

Sections 368 and 201 were added to the case on these grounds.

Medical examinations of the complainants were conducted, and their statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were recorded before a magistrate.

The incomplete investigation report further stated that DNA, fingerprint and polygraph tests had also been conducted, while call data records had been obtained.

It added that the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s reports were still awaited. Therefore, the police submitted an incomplete investigation report to avoid delays, despite having sufficient evidence against the suspects.

The police asked the court to summon the suspects through notices.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal has already distributed copies of the police report among the suspects and fixed Nov 11 for the next hearing.

Advocate Salman Shahid, defence counsel for two of the suspects charged with sexual assault, accused the police of favouring the key suspects in its investigation. He claimed that his clients were low-paid employees of one of the key suspects and had been made scapegoats.

One of his clients was a member of the janitorial staff at the property where the alleged incident took place, he added.

In July, Lahore Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Operations Faisal Kamran said that the police had been ordered to treat a suspect — reportedly linked to a senior government minister — in the case like “any other criminal”.

DIG Kamran had recounted the events leading up to the recovery of the women and the subsequent arrest of the suspects in a press conference. He said that during the investigation it had emerged that a “criminal gang” may have been behind the incident.

He further vowed that the police would ensure no legal loophole — which could be exploited in favour of the suspect — was left.

The two women departed Pakistan on July 3.

article_html:
LAHORE: An incomplete investigation report (challan) filed before a trial court in connection with the alleged gang rape of two foreign women in July cleared five suspects, including one reportedly linked to a senior minister, of sexual assault charges.

However, the report implicated them in other offences, including illegal detention and extortion.

The police charged three other suspects, who were allegedly low-paid employees of one of the key suspects, with sexually assaulting the women.

Defence C police registered the first information report (FIR) under Sections 365-A (kidnapping or abducting for extorting property, valuable security), 375-A (rape), 201 (causing disappearance of evidence of offence), 368 (wrongfully concealing or keeping in confinement, kidnapped or abducted person) and 337-L (II) (punishment for other hurt) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC) in July.

The investigation report said the two complainants alleged that they had met one of the three prime suspects in Singapore in 2025 and invited him to invest in their cryptocurrency business.

After receiving returns on his initial investment, he invested a further $500,000. However, according to the police report, the women did not pay him any profits or return his investment this time.

In June this year, the suspect invited the foreign women to Pakistan on the pretext of arranging a meeting with another investor. They stayed at a hotel in Islamabad and travelled to Murree and other areas.

The investigation report alleged that the suspect subsequently told an associate that the women owed him money. The associate then involved another prime suspect, identified as “boss”.

On June 29, the women were taken to a house in Defence Phase VII, Lahore, where they were allegedly detained and pressured to pay the amount.

Police said the women were forced to transfer around $19,500, which was converted into rupees through a Lahore-based account. Of this amount, Rs1.1 million each reportedly went to two of the suspects.

According to the report submitted to the court, the women alleged that armed men guarded them at the house, threatened them with a knife, a gun and a piece of broken mirror, and warned that they would be killed and their body parts sold if they failed to meet the demands.

The report said the complainants’ statements and the investigation indicated that three suspects had committed sexual assault. Police said they found no evidence of rape against the other five suspects, including the relative of the political figure and the suspect identified as “boss”.

The report further stated that the women escaped on July 1 when a car taking them to the airport met with an accident near Bhatta Chowk.

They raised an alarm, following which the relative of the senior political figure fled, and the police took the women into their protection.

Police also claimed to have recovered Rs4.3 million allegedly extorted from the women, along with a mobile phone and a vehicle allegedly used in the crime. Pistols and a rifle were also recovered, leading to the registration of separate cases under the Arms Ordinance, the report added.

Another suspect was accused of renting the house to the group without informing the authorities, while a further suspect was allegedly involved in helping to destroy evidence.

Sections 368 and 201 were added to the case on these grounds.

Medical examinations of the complainants were conducted, and their statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure were recorded before a magistrate.

The incomplete investigation report further stated that DNA, fingerprint and polygraph tests had also been conducted, while call data records had been obtained.

It added that the Punjab Forensic Science Agency’s reports were still awaited. Therefore, the police submitted an incomplete investigation report to avoid delays, despite having sufficient evidence against the suspects.

The police asked the court to summon the suspects through notices.

Additional District and Sessions Judge Rafaqat Ali Gondal has already distributed copies of the police report among the suspects and fixed Nov 11 for the next hearing.

Advocate Salman Shahid, defence counsel for two of the suspects charged with sexual assault, accused the police of favouring the key suspects in its investigation. He claimed that his clients were low-paid employees of one of the key suspects and had been made scapegoats.

One of his clients was a member of the janitorial staff at the property where the alleged incident took place, he added.

In July, Lahore Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Operations Faisal Kamran said that the police had been ordered to treat a suspect — reportedly linked to a senior government minister — in the case like “any other criminal”.

DIG Kamran had recounted the events leading up to the recovery of the women and the subsequent arrest of the suspects in a press conference. He said that during the investigation it had emerged that a “criminal gang” may have been behind the incident.

He further vowed that the police would ensure no legal loophole — which could be exploited in favour of the suspect — was left.

The two women departed Pakistan on July 3.

article_text:
Iran unveiled a massive billboard and banners pledging to kill US President Donald Trump across Tehran, bringing to a new level the official rhetoric displayed in the capital, AFP reports.

“We will kill Trump”, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran, which depicted the US president behind bars with his head bowed, according to the report.

headline: Six months of record-breaking development: Union Town offers fully developed, possession-ready plots on Pine Avenue
description: Union Town announces six months of major infrastructure development, with possession-ready residential and commercial plots.
author: ADVERTORIAL
article_text:
Union Town, an LDA-approved, master-planned community developed by Union Developers (Pvt.) Limited, has achieved significant development milestones, with major infrastructure works completed and residential and commercial plots ready for possession.

Ideally located in the Heart of Urban Lahore, Union Town offers triple access via Kadir Topbas Chowk, Abdul Sattar Edhi Road, and Khayaban-e-Jinnah, ensuring seamless connectivity to key areas of the city.

Its position within the city places key landmarks within minutes’ drive, including: 2 minutes to M2 Motorway, 3 minutes to Shaukat Khanum Hospital & UCP, while just 5 minutes to Lahore Ring Road and Canal Road.

Within 6 months of record-breaking development, Union Town has witnessed record-breaking progress, marked by the completion of infrastructure works, including internal road networks, streetlights, and the installation of a sewerage system.

A key feature of the community is its 150-feet-wide Pine Avenue, a signal-free corridor that runs directly through Union Town, providing access to every block. Alongside its possession-ready residential plots, Union Town offers fully developed commercials facing Pine Avenue, creating opportunities for retail, commercial activities, and business investment within a growing urban community.

Union Town reflects Union Developers’ commitment to delivering well-planned communities that combine residential and commercial opportunities under its vision of Buland Mayar-e-Zindagi.

Speaking about the project’s vision, Union Developers CEO Naeem Ahmad Malik said, “Union Town reflects our commitment to delivering a quality lifestyle through thoughtful planning, modern infrastructure, and a community designed to serve generations to come.”

With residential plots ranging from 3 to 20 Marla and commercial plots from 2 to 10 Marla, Union Town offers opportunities for people from different walks of life, creating a setting that caters to diverse lifestyle needs and investment aspirations.

With fully developed infrastructure, possession-ready plots, community parks and signal-free Pine Avenue, Union Town becomes the only kind of community that not only enhances present needs but guarantees a successful future tomorrow.

Qatar has said it remained hopeful that a deal could be reached between the US and Iran as both sides review proposals put forward by mediators including Doha, according to AFP.

“Both parties remain committed to the negotiation process; as we mentioned, we are facilitating the real-time exchange of proposals between them,” foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari told reporters, while adding that both sides “are currently reviewing the ideas and proposals we have presented”.

headline: Instagram Posts
Petitions against detention of Sohail Afridi, others referred to PHC CJ for constitution of larger bench
description: “These are not ordinary personalities,” remarks Justice Ali during the hearing; KP AG seeks three days to submit replies.
author: Waseem Ahmad Shah
article_text:
PESHAWAR: A Peshawar High Court (PHC) bench on Tuesday referred multiple petitions challenging the detention of PTI leaders, including Sohail Afridi — the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister — to the chief justice for the constitution of a larger bench.

Afridi has not been seen since the imposition of governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11. His whereabouts remained unknown on the day governor’s rule was imposed, and a federal minister confirmed a day later that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody.

The PTI has also alleged the detention and arrests of several of its other members, including lawmakers and ministers. Their whereabouts have not been disclosed by the government so far.

Multiple pleas have been filed in the PHC in this connection. A division bench comprising Justice Syed Arshad Ali and Justice Muhammad Faheem Wali took up the petitions on Tuesday.

Apart from Afridi’s detention, the petitions also pertain to the alleged disappearance of KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, MNAs Junaid Akbar and Dr Amjid Ali, provincial minister Amjid Ali Khan, MPAs Ikramullah and Aurangzeb Khan, former chief minister of Gilgit-Baltistan Mohammad Khalid Khursheed and several other PTI leaders.

Afridi’s brother Mohammad Aamir filed one of the petitions, alleging that Afridi was “abducted” from Chief Minister House on the night that the emergency was imposed in the province. He had approached the PHC on Oct 13.

On Tuesday, the bench referred the pleas to the chief justice after the KP government and senior police officials failed to file their respective replies in accordance with the court’s Oct 20 directives.

“These are not ordinary personalities,” remarked Justice Ali during the hearing.

Meanwhile, KP Advocate General Sanaullah Khan sought three days to submit the replies, adding that his office was awaiting a response from the provincial home department, police and other law enforcement agencies.

Bashir Vazir, who appeared on behalf of the petitioners, alleged that the PTI leaders had been missing for many days. He contended that, under Article 199 of the Constitution, the PHC had authority to order that Afridi and Swati be produced before the court.

He further argued that the KP Assembly had passed an immunity law under which a member of the assembly could not be arrested in such manner, adding that the assembly’s speaker also could not be arrested under the law.

The law stipulated that the speaker would remain in office until a successor is elected, Vazir said.

According to the KP advocate general, in more than 200 instances of detentions under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance (MPO), orders were passed without the cases being heard.

The bench disagreed with the claim, observing that in those cases reports had been sought from the respondents but were never submitted. It further observed that the detentions under consideration were not MPO cases.

“This is an important case; the chief minister of the province is missing,” Justice Ali observed.

The bench said the court had given the respondents 10 days to file replies, but they had not complied with the order.

“We refer this case to the chief justice to constitute a larger bench,” Justice Ali said. The KP advocate general also requested the constitution of a larger bench.

headline: Reels
IHC suspends order rejecting FIR plea in Pims fire case, seeks inquiry report and govt response
description: Court issues notices to federal government, Prime Minister's Office among others.
author: Malik Asad
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order dismissing an application seeking the registration of an FIR into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) neonatal fire tragedy.

The court also directed the authorities to submit the complete record, along with the inquiry report, and issued notices to the respondents, including the federal government and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability, with criminal action being ordered against eight officials.

“I will call for all reports and summon all evidence,” Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro observed while hearing a petition filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi on behalf of The Jurists Foundation of Pakistan.

“If any negligence comes to light, I will order the registration of a case against those responsible,” the judge added.

The petition seeks the registration of an FIR in connection with the deaths of 14 newborns in a fire at the Gynaecology Ward/Special Care Centre of the Mother and Child Hospital (MCH) at Pims.

The petitioner alleged that the incident was caused by gross negligence, including the absence of staff from a ward that had reportedly been locked to prevent theft.

Earlier, on Aug 28, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an inquiry against eight Pims officials over alleged negligence in addressing fire-safety deficiencies. The report alleged that the officials failed to take timely corrective measures despite being alerted to safety shortcomings, and that the subsequent tragedy could have been prevented.

“In the Pims tragedy, 14 children were burned simultaneously,” he said, adding that “even among wild animals in the jungle, such a thing does not happen,” said the counsel.

Justice Soomro, however, asked the counsel to restrict his submissions to the legal aspects of the case. When Rahi continued narrating details of the tragedy, the judge remarked: “You are veering off track again; please present legal arguments pertaining to your case.”

The counsel argued that no FIR had been registered in the deaths to date. The judge asked whether an inquiry had been conducted. Rahi replied that the inquiry report had established negligence and urged the court to direct the registration of an FIR before the end of the court’s working hours.

Explaining the delay, the counsel said the Justice of the Peace had dismissed his application on the grounds that petitions relating to the matter were already pending before the high court.

He argued that, apart from him, no one else had approached the police station seeking the registration of a case and that an FIR should have been registered.

“I have gathered so much evidence — but if an FIR is not registered, where am I supposed to take this evidence?” he asked.

After hearing the arguments, the court suspended the Justice of the Peace’s order and directed the authorities to submit the complete record, including the inquiry reports, before the next hearing. It also directed that all evidence be placed on record.

Other prayers

The petition, filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, also seeks directions for the respondents to compensate the victims’ families under Section 323 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

It further asks the court to restrain government medical staff, including doctors, from engaging in private practice, particularly at commercial establishments, unless permitted under a validly framed law.

Among other reliefs sought, the petitioner has asked the court to direct the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority to include individuals such as Dr Khaliq-uz-Zaman in its governing body, ensure that the relevant institutions meet ISO standards and direct the Auditor General to submit audit reports. In the event of any discrepancies, the petition seeks directions for the FIA to initiate proceedings.

The petition also calls for the replacement of expired electrical wiring in government hospitals. It further seeks a declaration that placing newborns in isolation is unreasonable, illogical and illegal, and runs counter to maternal love.

It further asks the court to declare the construction of the Mother and Child Hospital an encroachment on the hospital’s already approved plan and direct that the neonatal units be reconfigured so newborns can be placed within sight of their mothers and close to their beds.

The petitioner has also sought compensatory costs for filing the public interest litigation.

The court issued notices to the federal government through the Cabinet secretary, the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Interior, the Establishment Division, the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council, the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, the Auditor General of Pakistan, the Islamabad chief commissioner and deputy commissioner, the Capital Development Authority, Capital Emergency Services, the executive director of Pims, the Islamabad inspector general of police, the SSP Operations, the FIA director general and other respondents, seeking their replies.

The hearing was adjourned until Nov 12.

article_html:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday suspended a Justice of the Peace’s order dismissing an application seeking the registration of an FIR into the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) neonatal fire tragedy.

The court also directed the authorities to submit the complete record, along with the inquiry report, and issued notices to the respondents, including the federal government and the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability, with criminal action being ordered against eight officials.

“I will call for all reports and summon all evidence,” Justice Khadim Hussain Soomro observed while hearing a petition filed by lawyer Riaz Hanif Rahi on behalf of The Jurists Foundation of Pakistan.

“If any negligence comes to light, I will order the registration of a case against those responsible,” the judge added.

The petition seeks the registration of an FIR in connection with the deaths of 14 newborns in a fire at the Gynaecology Ward/Special Care Centre of the Mother and Child Hospital (MCH) at Pims.

The petitioner alleged that the incident was caused by gross negligence, including the absence of staff from a ward that had reportedly been locked to prevent theft.

Earlier, on Aug 28, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ordered an inquiry against eight Pims officials over alleged negligence in addressing fire-safety deficiencies. The report alleged that the officials failed to take timely corrective measures despite being alerted to safety shortcomings, and that the subsequent tragedy could have been prevented.

“In the Pims tragedy, 14 children were burned simultaneously,” he said, adding that “even among wild animals in the jungle, such a thing does not happen,” said the counsel.

Justice Soomro, however, asked the counsel to restrict his submissions to the legal aspects of the case. When Rahi continued narrating details of the tragedy, the judge remarked: “You are veering off track again; please present legal arguments pertaining to your case.”

The counsel argued that no FIR had been registered in the deaths to date. The judge asked whether an inquiry had been conducted. Rahi replied that the inquiry report had established negligence and urged the court to direct the registration of an FIR before the end of the court’s working hours.

Explaining the delay, the counsel said the Justice of the Peace had dismissed his application on the grounds that petitions relating to the matter were already pending before the high court.

He argued that, apart from him, no one else had approached the police station seeking the registration of a case and that an FIR should have been registered.

“I have gathered so much evidence — but if an FIR is not registered, where am I supposed to take this evidence?” he asked.

After hearing the arguments, the court suspended the Justice of the Peace’s order and directed the authorities to submit the complete record, including the inquiry reports, before the next hearing. It also directed that all evidence be placed on record.

Other prayers

The petition, filed under Article 199 of the Constitution, also seeks directions for the respondents to compensate the victims’ families under Section 323 of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC).

It further asks the court to restrain government medical staff, including doctors, from engaging in private practice, particularly at commercial establishments, unless permitted under a validly framed law.

Among other reliefs sought, the petitioner has asked the court to direct the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority to include individuals such as Dr Khaliq-uz-Zaman in its governing body, ensure that the relevant institutions meet ISO standards and direct the Auditor General to submit audit reports. In the event of any discrepancies, the petition seeks directions for the FIA to initiate proceedings.

The petition also calls for the replacement of expired electrical wiring in government hospitals. It further seeks a declaration that placing newborns in isolation is unreasonable, illogical and illegal, and runs counter to maternal love.

It further asks the court to declare the construction of the Mother and Child Hospital an encroachment on the hospital’s already approved plan and direct that the neonatal units be reconfigured so newborns can be placed within sight of their mothers and close to their beds.

The petitioner has also sought compensatory costs for filing the public interest litigation.

The court issued notices to the federal government through the Cabinet secretary, the Prime Minister’s Office, the Ministry of Interior, the Establishment Division, the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council, the Islamabad Healthcare Regulatory Authority, the Auditor General of Pakistan, the Islamabad chief commissioner and deputy commissioner, the Capital Development Authority, Capital Emergency Services, the executive director of Pims, the Islamabad inspector general of police, the SSP Operations, the FIA director general and other respondents, seeking their replies.

The hearing was adjourned until Nov 12.

headline: French judges probe war crimes complaint against Israeli army in Lebanon: lawyer
description: The crimes against humanity unit of the Paris Judicial Court has appointed two investigating judges to the case.
author: AFP
article_text:
France has opened a judicial investigation into a war crimes complaint over an Israeli strike on a residential building in Lebanon, a lawyer told AFP on Tuesday.

French-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri, whose parents were killed in the Beirut strike in 2024, filed the complaint as a civil party this year with the International Federation for Human Rights, Cherri’s lawyer Clemence Bectarte explained.

The crimes against humanity unit of the Paris Judicial Court has appointed two investigating judges to the case, she added, hailing the move as “a first”.

Hezbollah fought with Israel at the start of the war on Gaza following the events of October 7, 2023.

The hostilities, which escalated into open war in September 2024, have left more than 4,000 dead in Lebanon and forced more than a million people to flee.

Seven civilians, including Cherri’s father and mother, aged 87 and 77, were killed in the bombing of their 12-storey apartment building in central Beirut on November 26, 2024, according to the complaint seen by AFP. Three floors were destroyed.

The strike occurred “just a few hours before the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah came into effect,” the complaint stated, citing detailed research by Amnesty International and Forensic Architecture into the incident.

AFP has reached out to the Israeli military for comment.

Cherri told AFP he had taken legal action “for the dignity of all civilian victims”.

“For nearly two years, I have been fighting… to ensure that the Israeli bombing that killed my parents and five other civilians does not go unpunished,” he said.

“What happened to my parents is not an isolated case… I hope this investigation will help break the impunity enjoyed by Israeli officials responsible for attacks against civilians in Lebanon and Palestine,” he added.

Several investigations underway

While the judicial investigation marks a first over alleged war crimes by Israeli forces in Lebanon, other cases are pending.

French-Lebanese man Mohamad H., represented by lawyer Emmanuel Daoud, has sought action after losing his mother, sister, and two nephews in strikes on the southern city of Tyre during the night of April 16-17.

In another case, a French entrepreneur born in Lebanon has accused the Israeli army of uprooting 600-century-old olive trees belonging to his family in a village in southern Lebanon.

France’s National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT), which handles war crimes, has opened an investigation into allegations of torture and war crimes related to the Israeli forces’ interception of humanitarian flotillas bound for Gaza in 2025 and 2026.

The PNAT also asked a Paris judge to open a war crimes investigation into the deaths of two French children in an Israeli bombing in Gaza in October 2023, while ruling out charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, according to sources close to the case.

In another case, a French entrepreneur born in Lebanon has accused the Israeli army of uprooting 600-century-old olive trees belonging to his family in a village in southern Lebanon.

France’s National Anti-Terrorism Prosecutor’s Office (PNAT), which handles war crimes, has opened an investigation into allegations of torture and war crimes related to the Israeli forces’ interception of humanitarian flotillas bound for Gaza in 2025 and 2026.

The PNAT also asked a Paris judge to open a war crimes investigation into the deaths of two French children in an Israeli bombing in Gaza in October 2023, while ruling out charges of genocide and crimes against humanity, according to sources close to the case.

headline: IHC grants protective bail to TikToker booked following stampede at wedding event
description: Justice Dogar allows the suspect time to approach the relevant forum, preventing his arrest till November 10; Jatt appears before the court in a wheelchair.
author: Malik Asad
article_text:
ISLAMABAD: The Islamabad High Court (IHC) on Tuesday granted protective bail to TikToker Muhammad Ansar Jatt, alias “Mr Pattlo”, after a stampede at his mehndi (henna) event in Sialkot claimed two lives.

Jatt had announced holding a mehndi event and prize-distribution ceremony at Faraz Cricket Ground on Daska Road on Friday night; however, with hundreds gathered at the site, a stampede occurred when the stadium gates opened, killing two and injuring 18 people.

Subsequently, a first information report (FIR) was registered on October 31 at the Motra Police Station, naming Jatt, his brother, the owner of Faraz Cricket Ground, six others, and 40-45 unidentified security guards.

On Tuesday, IHC Chief Justice Sardar Muhammad Sarfraz Dogar approved the protective — also known as transitory — bail for the TikToker until Nov 10, allowing him to avoid arrest while he approaches the relevant court to seek legal remedy. He surrendered before the court in a wheelchair.

Jatt had filed a petition, seeking the court’s intervention to prevent his arrest before he could reach the court of competent jurisdiction. Advocates Barrister Qasim Nawaz Abbasi and Barrister Raja Ali Abbas Jalap filed the petition on his behalf.

According to the legal document, Jatt was named in the FIR, which was registered under Sections 322 (punishment for qatl-i-khata), 440 (mischief committed after preparation made for causing death or hurt), 431 (mischief by injury to public road, bridge, river or channel), 148 (rioting, armed with deadly weapon), 149 (unlawful assembly), 188 (disobedience to order duly promulgated by public servant) and 109 (punishment of abetment) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC), read with Section 16 of the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960.

During the proceedings, the petitioner’s counsel argued that the FIR was registered outside the IHC’s territorial jurisdiction. However, the counsel maintained that the sole object of seeking protective bail was to enable a suspect present within the jurisdiction of one court to safely approach the court where the case was registered without being arrested on the way.

“The merits of the case are not required to be examined at this stage,” the petition stated, adding that without the protection, the petitioner’s right to seek pre-arrest bail before a Sialkot court would be rendered illusory.

The petition further contended that the allegations levelled against the petitioner were “false, frivolous, and baseless,” claiming that he had been falsely implicated.

It was also brought to the court’s notice that the petitioner had no previous criminal record and that no other petition seeking the same relief had been filed before any other court.

After hearing the arguments, Justice Dogar granted the relief, noting the temporary and limited nature of the protective bail and allowing the petitioner time to surrender before the appropriate forum.

On Sunday, Sialkot police said they had arrested six suspects in relation to the incident.

Police said Jatt immediately fled the scene after the incident, adding that their investigation and raid teams were conducting operations to apprehend the TikTok influencer. Sialkot District Police Officer Dost Muhammad confirmed that the six arrested individuals were involved in managing the event.

According to the DPO, organisers had invited a large number of people by advertising a lucky draw featuring prizes such as motorcycles, a car and other valuable items via social media.

During the event, an announcement was made over the loudspeakers instructing all attendees to enter the grounds simultaneously. This simultaneous entry into the sports stadium triggered a severe stampede, the DPO said.

He stated that the organisers violated the terms of their permit, as well as established safety standard operating procedures (SOPs). The stampede also disrupted the flow of traffic on the main Daska-Sialkot Road.

The Sialkot DPO declared that legal action would be taken against all those responsible for the incident, without any discrimination.

headline: Saudi Aramco profits surge as Middle East war rattles energy markets
description: Saudi oil giant Aramco announced a 34.6 per cent surge in third-quarter net profit, as the Middle East war keeps...
article_text:
Saudi oil giant Aramco announced a 34.6 per cent surge in third-quarter net profit, as the Middle East war keeps crude prices soaring while the kingdom’s energy infrastructure comes under regular attack, AFP reports.

Yemen’s Houthis have targeted Saudi tankers, pipelines, storage facilities and refineries regularly since hostilities resumed in July, intensifying their strikes in recent weeks.

The firm said net profit hit 135.9 billion riyals ($36.2bn) in the third quarter, compared with around 101bn riyals in the same period a year earlier.

But Aramco’s boss warned that the conflict continued to weigh heavily on energy security.

In the second quarter, Aramco had reported a 44pc year-on-year increase in net profit to 122.6bn riyals.

headline: How necessity continues to be the mother of invention in Pakistan
description: How can solar power be used to address issues around commuting, cooking and obtaining drinking water?
author: Zil E Huma
article_text:
Nowadays, the sight of solar panels perched on rooftops has become commonplace in Pakistan. According to an analysis published by Renewables First and the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air earlier this year, Pakistan has gone from importing less than one gigawatt (GW) of solar modules in 2018 to more than 51GW by early 2026. It estimated that the boom had already spared the country more than $12 billion in oil and gas imports by February.

For a country long held hostage to load-shedding and rising tariffs, rooftop panels are a manifestation of the age-old adage: necessity is the mother of invention.

But it appears that the boom has outrun the system built to absorb it. In 2026, the power regulator moved from “net metering” to “net-billing”, under which solar prosumers buy power from the grid at standard retail rates but sell excess solar energy back at a much lower rate.

The shift has raised demand for batteries as households and businesses look to store the power they generate instead of selling it back to the government. It also shows how the energy of the sun can be harnessed in ways to address the plethora of issues the people of the country are facing.

At the recently held Solar Pakistan Exhibition in Karachi — which brought together solar technology, solar power solutions, renewable energy innovations and sustainable energy products — innovation was in full display. Specifically, it showed how to use solar power to address issues around commuting, cooking and obtaining drinking water.

Battery-swapping stations for electric vehicles

With the US-Israeli war on Iran and its effects on global oil prices showing no signs of abating, electric vehicles (EVs) have now started trickling onto the roads in Pakistan. According to a recent Dawn report, around 150,000 electric bikes and scooties were sold across the country in 2025.

The report, however, noted that despite this, EV sales were still not comparable to motorcycle sales: a CD70 costs Rs168,000, while a proper lithium-powered electric bike costs more than Rs300,000.

At the Solar Pakistan Exhibition held on October 10, Bahum Global PVT, a solar service company, introduced its EV bikes with a unique answer to both the cost and the battery degradation problem: battery-swapping stations.

One problem EV owners have complained of is the battery “dying” like that of a phone, which makes many wary of being stranded en route.

To cater to this issue, Zafar Khan, the general manager of Bahum, told Dawn that the company is in talks with petrol pump brands like Pakistan State Oil (PSO), Shell and Total to install battery-swapping stations. The electric bikes themselves will be manufactured in Pakistan, which will hopefully cut the taxation costs as well.

This way, instead of leaving the battery on charge overnight or having to abruptly halt a journey due to the battery running out of charge, an EV owner can stop at a nearby petrol pump with a swapping facility and exchange the drained battery for one that is charged one at a fixed cost.

After a successful pilot at the PSO petrol pump in Lahore’s Cantt area, Bahum is set to launch the EVs and battery-swapping stations throughout Pakistan in December 2026.

Rocket Choolha

It is the story of every household: cooking gas vanishes from the kitchens like a wisp of smoke into the night as soon as the clock strikes nine. Many have resorted to using gas cylinders to cook at their own convenience instead of the government’s. This is where Rocket Choolha comes in: a product by Mesol Solar aiming to provide a safe and eco-friendly way to keep the burners on.

Based on the concept of a biomass stove, the choolha utilises wood pellets created in-house by recycling wood waste. All moisture is extracted from the waste before it is turned into lightweight pellets. These pellets serve as the main fuel for the choolha, providing users with a solution costing almost half of what they spend on LPG — which is susceptible to price fluctuations during times of high demand.

All one has to do is top up the steel cylinder inside the choolha with wood pellets, add a few drops of kerosene (it can work if you omit oil as well), and light the pellets on fire. The design comes with an attached regulator to control the intensity of the flame; all you need to do is charge the choolha with your phone charger or a battery pack — which could further reduce costs if it is solar powered. The interior is lined with glass fibre, a heat-resistant material also used in protective gear for firefighters, which, according to Mesol Solar, makes the appliance safe to use at home.

For now, the Rocket choolha is far from a replacement for the gas line that gives out just as one begins to think of stepping into the kitchen. But it does something clever: it takes what would have been wood waste swept into a corner and turns it into a means for making dinner. Nothing is felled for the fire; the wood has simply been given a second shift.

Extracting water through the air

With a burgeoning population, Pakistan faces growing pressure on its resources, especially clean drinking water. But what if that could be addressed by something that is available in abundance, like the air? A Nippon Energy product, SkySip is a water-dispenser look-alike entirely powered by solar, making it an end-to-end environmentally friendly product.

All it requires is a solar panel and an inverter to convert DC power from the solar panels to AC. The unit then uses clean solar power to draw ambient air, which is cooled to condense moisture into water droplets. The collected water then passes through a series of filters to purify it and make it safe to drink.

The range is what keeps SkySip from being a novelty. Although the units haven’t been rolled out in Pakistan yet, the smallest is rated to produce 20 litres a day, enough for a small household or shop. The bigger models climb from 50 litres to 1,000 litres a day, which makes the range suitable for everything from homes and offices to restaurants and industries. Power demand climbs with output, from 250 to 350 watts for the smallest unit to 4.5 to 6 kilowatts for the largest.

It won’t replace the pipeline or the tanker. But for clinics, schools and far-flung communities where water is scarce, unsafe or sold at a premium, a machine that turns sunlight and air into a glass of drinking water is a lifeline of a different kind.

None of these products are ready to replace what we rely on. However, other than powering households, they show the different ways in which Pakistan can innovate to harness a power it possesses in abundance.

These pellets serve as the main fuel for the choolha, providing users with a solution costing almost half of what they spend on LPG — which is susceptible to price fluctuations during times of high demand.

All one has to do is top up the steel cylinder inside the choolha with wood pellets, add a few drops of kerosene (it can work if you omit oil as well), and light the pellets on fire. The design comes with an attached regulator to control the intensity of the flame; all you need to do is charge the choolha with your phone charger or a battery pack — which could further reduce costs if it is solar powered. The interior is lined with glass fibre, a heat-resistant material also used in protective gear for firefighters, which, according to Mesol Solar, makes the appliance safe to use at home.

For now, the Rocket choolha is far from a replacement for the gas line that gives out just as one begins to think of stepping into the kitchen. But it does something clever: it takes what would have been wood waste swept into a corner and turns it into a means for making dinner. Nothing is felled for the fire; the wood has simply been given a second shift.
Extracting water through the air

With a burgeoning population, Pakistan faces growing pressure on its resources, especially clean drinking water. But what if that could be addressed by something that is available in abundance, like the air? A Nippon Energy product, SkySip is a water-dispenser look-alike entirely powered by solar, making it an end-to-end environmentally friendly product.

All it requires is a solar panel and an inverter to convert DC power from the solar panels to AC. The unit then uses clean solar power to draw ambient air, which is cooled to condense moisture into water droplets. The collected water then passes through a series of filters to purify it and make it safe to drink.

The range is what keeps SkySip from being a novelty. Although the units haven’t been rolled out in Pakistan yet, the smallest is rated to produce 20 litres a day, enough for a small household or shop. The bigger models climb from 50 litres to 1,000 litres a day, which makes the range suitable for everything from homes and offices to restaurants and industries. Power demand climbs with output, from 250 to 350 watts for the smallest unit to 4.5 to 6 kilowatts for the largest.

It won’t replace the pipeline or the tanker. But for clinics, schools and far-flung communities where water is scarce, unsafe or sold at a premium, a machine that turns sunlight and air into a glass of drinking water is a lifeline of a different kind.

None of these products are ready to replace what we rely on. However, other than powering households, they show the different ways in which Pakistan can innovate to harness a power it possesses in abundance.

Iranian deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi has said that Tehran reserved the right to self-defence following US attacks on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz, AFP reports, citing Iran’s ISNA news agency

“The Islamic Republic of Iran retains the right to legitimate self-defence until the military aggression has been completely and permanently brought to an end,” Gharibabadi said.

headline: Lahore court grants NCCIA further two-day remand of suspects over US postage stamp fraud
description: IO's request for another 5-day remand of prime suspect, co-suspect denied.
author: Wajih Ahmad Sheikh
article_text:
LAHORE: A judicial magistrate on Tuesday granted the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) a further two-day physical remand of two suspects in a Rs35 billion fraud involving the online sale of counterfeit US postage stamps.

The prime suspect, identified as a 33-year-old resident of Khanewal, had been charged by a Florida jury with defrauding the United States Postal Service (USPS) of $126 million, the US Attorney’s Office of the Southern District of Florida said on Sept 28.

The Lahore NCCIA announced the prime suspect’s arrest in late October, and he was sent on a five-day physical remand on Oct 21. Today’s extension of the physical remand is the third for him, and second for the co-suspect.

On Tuesday, the NCCIA produced both men before Judicial Magistrate Naeem Wattoo upon the expiry of their latest four-day remand.

The investigating officer (IO) sought custody of the suspects for another five days for interrogation.

However, Magistrate Wattoo granted the agency two more days of physical custody and directed the IO to produce the suspects again on Nov 5.

According to NCCIA, the initial investigation revealed that the prime suspect operated a website to market and sell over 5m fake US postage stamps over a period of more than three years.

According to the US Department of Justice, the website run by the Pakistani national was not authorised to sell USPS products and services.

The counterfeit labels allegedly allowed customers to ship packages at rates “far below legitimate USPS prices”, it said, adding that it caused losses exceeding $126m to the postal service.

US prosecutors alleged that the website sold the labels for around $2 each, regardless of a package’s weight, size or destination. A US court order authorised the seizure and shutdown of the website.

Money trail

In a press conference on Oct 20, NCCIA’s Lahore Zone Additional Director Atif Ameer said that 16 bank accounts had been used in the scam. Seven of the accounts were operated by the suspect, five by his brother, two by his wife, and one each by his sister and aunt.

He said the agency had expanded the investigation across several parts of the country.

“Eight special teams were formed in Punjab, Islamabad and Sindh to trace the suspect and investigate the network,” he said and added the teams conducted raids at 35 locations and questioned 47 people as part of the investigation.

“Investigators also employed digital and forensic techniques to establish the suspect’s movements and identify people associated with the operation.”

Ameer added that investigators analysed 122 call-data records, 50 IMEI-tracking reports and audio and video recordings from 120 cameras.

“Artificial intelligence and other modern technological tools were also used during the investigation. A locator operation continued for 10 days as investigators attempted to establish the suspect’s whereabouts and trace his activities,” he said.

The NCCIA said the major focus of the investigation was the financial trail generated by the online sale of the counterfeit stamps.

“We are examining transactions conducted through the 16 bank accounts and attempting to determine the flow of funds between the accounts allegedly belonging to the suspect and his relatives.

“The involvement of family members is also being examined as part of the investigation, particularly the alleged use of their bank accounts in connection with the online business,” the additional director said.

He said the role of other individuals in operating the website, processing orders, receiving payments or distributing the counterfeit stamps was also being probed.

“Investigators are also working to establish the full scale of the operation and verify the volume and value of the transactions,” he said.

headline: Iran outlines 5 conditions for regional security
description: Iran’s top military commander has outlined five conditions for establishing lasting security, according to Anadolu....
article_text:
Iran’s top military commander has outlined five conditions for establishing lasting security, according to Anadolu.

Major General Ali Abdollahi, Chief of Staff of Iran’s Armed Forces and commander of the Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, is quoted by state broadcaster IRIB as saying that Iran has emerged as a “fourth centre of global power” through its control of the Strait of Hormuz and its ability to determine the rules governing access to the waterway.

Abdollahi outlines five conditions that Tehran considers essential for establishing lasting security:

Ending wars on all fronts, particularly in Lebanon and the Gaza Strip, while rejecting negotiations conducted under military threats
The complete lifting of sanctions against Iran and the release of frozen Iranian assets
Compensation for damage caused by the US-Israeli war on Iran, as well as the 12-day war with Israel last year
Recognition of Iran’s sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz and the replacement of the US-led security framework with what Abdolahi describes as a “Hormuz mechanism”
Guarantees against renewed military attacks and the establishment of security arrangements led by countries in the region.

Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian said that a resumption of fighting with the United States would not benefit anyone, reiterating that his government had been granted fresh negotiating powers in exchanges with Washington, AFP reports.

headline: Iran 'not in a good negotiating position': Trump
description: US President Donald Trump says that Iran is “not in a good negotiating position”, while denying that the conflict is...
article_text:
US President Donald Trump says that Iran is “not in a good negotiating position”, while denying that the conflict is a “war”.

“What’s a war? A war is fighting … When was the last time you saw us fighting with them?” he tells Fox News. “We go months and months; we talk. They’re not in a good negotiating position; their economy is cratering … they have 301 per cent inflation; they don’t have money.”

He adds that the war could go on if no agreement is made, but stresses that Iran wants “to make a deal really badly” and that there is a “very good chance” of a deal being struck.

“We’re dealing from total strength,“ Trump says.

headline: Soaring LPG prices force rickshaw drivers in Pakistan to cut meals
description: Thousands of drivers run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly used for cooking and heating.
author: Reuters
article_text:
For 13 years, Rashid Ali has driven a three-wheeled motorised rickshaw around Lahore.

His day starts at 6am and sometimes does not end until midnight, but he was long able to make around Rs1,700 ($6.50) a day, enough for his family’s bare essentials. Now, with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) prices surging, he doesn’t even make half that.

Ali, 33, is among thousands of drivers who run their vehicles on LPG, which is sold in cylinders and mainly used for cooking and heating.

Majeed Ghauri, Chairman of the Awami Rickshaw Union, calls it “the fuel of the poor” and says about 70 per cent of its members’ 43,000 auto-rickshaws and nearly 8,000 Qingqi motorcycle-based three-wheelers, which carry several passengers on set routes, run on LPG.

LPG prices have surged since October 17, when two Iranian border crossings closed, halting imports, traders say, in the latest energy shock since the US-Iran war began in February. One of the border crossings was opened a week later.

With Ali now lucky to make around Rs800 ($3) a day, his family has cut back on meals, eating only twice a day.

“Previously, when LPG was cheap, we could earn a decent income,” Ali said. “Now, it’s just not possible to get by on Rs700 or Rs800, is it?”

Before the border closures, Pakistan imported about 7,000 metric tonnes of LPG a day from Iran, the Pakistan LPG Association said.

Traders said the price of a 12-kilogramme cylinder jumped 56pc within days of the closure to Rs7,000, or about Rs583 rupees per kg in the open market.

Walking away

Ali pays Rs600 a day to rent his rickshaw, filling up with fuel four or five times a day, at Rs300 to Rs400 a time.

As well as daily expenses, Ali also pays Rs11,000 a month for his home and has two young children to support. Adding to his problems, passengers, he said, do not want to pay higher fares.

“For a trip that should cost Rs200 or Rs250, they might only offer Rs80, Rs100, or Rs150 rupees,” Ali said.

Passenger Mohammad Ramzan said when a driver asked Rs500 rupees for a ride in the city, he offered half that. When the driver declined, he walked away, he said.

Inflation hit 9.6pc in October and the central bank last week raised interest rates to 12pc, citing energy and wheat prices. Petrol hit a record Rs458 a litre on April 3 and remains about 40pc above its pre-war price.

Back home at midday, Ali said his two boys still needed their lunch. He would go out again until late at night, he said, hoping to make enough to bring something for the children to eat at night.

headline: Lufthansa latest airline to flag ticket price hikes amid Iran war energy shock
description: Lufthansa has become the latest airline to warn that ticket prices will rise further, as it forecast a...
article_text:
Lufthansa has become the latest airline to warn that ticket prices will rise further, as it forecast a two-billion-euro ($2.2 billion) jump in annual fuel costs due to the Middle East conflict, AFP reports.

It came a day after Irish no-frills carrier Ryanair said it would raise prices and launch a cost-cutting drive, as the US-Israeli war on Iran keeps global energy costs elevated.

The German firm, Europe’s biggest airline group by sales, said the outlook for fuel costs had worsened from just a few months ago, predicting a bill of 9.3bn euros for 2026, 2bn higher than last year.

Price hikes would be necessary “to pass on the increase in kerosene costs”, finance chief Till Streichert told journalists, after the group released forecast-beating quarterly results.

“Ticket prices will increase by double digits next year.”

He also warned fuel costs would increase in 2027, but added: “That can still change — and hopefully for the better — if the geopolitical situation eases.”
